comments.author: ccvannorman
comments.why: Covers known numbers and the quest to define normal numbers
comments.text: It's fascinating how little we know about everyday numbers like pi and e, it's widely assumed that they are normal but there is no proof for this (and it's extremely difficult to do so). In fact we believe the fast majority of numbers are transcendental and normal but we only actually know of a single normal number, and it is a manufactured number. Numberphile has an excellent video on the numbers we know about and the quest to find / define normal numbers: [VIDEO]

comments.author: jerf
comments.why: Shows we can name barely any of the numbers
comments.text: It's worse than you make it sound, though: [VIDEO] In short, it isn't just that we have more computables than non-computables; there are categories of numbers like "normal" that nominally contain "all the numbers" but we can barely even name a handful.
